presentation.label: FILTER HZ
presentation.summary: The FILTER page's FRQ and the FX track's DELAY HPF/LPF and REVERB FRQ/HPF/LPF show their frequency in hertz instead of 0 to 127.
presentation.overview: Filter Hz changes what the frequency knobs say. On the FILTER page FRQ shows the cutoff to three significant figures instead of the stock 0 to 127: 13.8Hz at 0, 440Hz at 60, 1.11kHz at 76 and 21.1kHz at 127, one semitone a step, from MrScruff's measurement of the self-oscillating filter. Since 1.3.0 the FX track does the same: DELAY and REVERB HPF and LPF and REVERB FRQ show the frequency the stock delay and reverb filters actually use, worked out on the unit from the coefficient the DSP reads. LPF follows HPF, as the stock filters do, and reads OPEN where the low-pass lets everything through. Only the display changes: the filters, their ranges, saved kits and every other parameter are untouched. A locked value's white box is 33 pixels instead of stock's 27, so kHz values fit. It is an elemod port of MrScruff's rytm-mods 0008-filter-hz, with his code unchanged; Modwerk adds the wider box (1.2.1) and the FX pages (1.3.0).
highlights: FILTER FRQ reads in Hz and kHz to three significant figures, 440Hz at the stock value 60.
DELAY HPF/LPF and REVERB FRQ/HPF/LPF read the frequency the stock FX filters use.
LPF follows HPF, locks included, and reads OPEN when the low-pass is fully open.
A locked value's white box is wide enough for kHz values.
Display only: the filters, their ranges and saved kits are unchanged.
usage: Use a build containing Filter Hz. Select a track and press FILTER to open its FILTER page.
Turn FRQ (knob E). The value popup reads the cutoff in hertz instead of 0 to 127: 440Hz at the stock value 60, one semitone a step.
Select the FX track and press SRC for DELAY or SMPL for REVERB. Turn HPF, LPF or the reverb's FRQ: each reads its frequency, and LPF reads OPEN above where the low-pass does anything.

access.location: Any track's FILTER page (FRQ, knob E), and the FX track's DELAY page (HPF E, LPF F) and REVERB page (FRQ C, HPF E, LPF F).
steps: Select a track and press FILTER, then turn FRQ (knob E).
Select the FX track and press SRC (DELAY) or SMPL (REVERB), then turn HPF, LPF or FRQ.

controls.name: Knob E — FRQ
controls.doc: Unchanged control. Its value popup shows the cutoff frequency, 13.8Hz at 0 to 21.1kHz at 127, one semitone a step, instead of the number.

controls.name: DELAY knobs E and F — HPF, LPF
controls.doc: Unchanged controls. HPF shows the delay's high-pass corner (-3 dB), 5.00Hz at 0 to 12.0kHz at 127; LPF shows the low-pass corner, which stock places from HPF + LPF, or OPEN when the low-pass has no -3 dB point below 24 kHz.

controls.name: REVERB knob C — FRQ
controls.doc: Unchanged control. Shows the corner of the reverb's treble shelf (the -3 dB point with GAI at 0), 974Hz at 0 to 14.0kHz at 127.

controls.name: REVERB knobs E and F — HPF, LPF
controls.doc: Unchanged controls. As the DELAY's: the same filters and scale.

limitations: Built for OS 1.74 only, with core-ar2 0.3. Version 1.2.0 drops the OS 1.73 release (core-ar2 0.1), which Modwerk no longer supports.
FILTER FRQ's scale was measured on the self-oscillating LP2 filter; the other filter types are assumed to share it.

Each value shows the knob's value, or the held trig's or scene's lock: envelope depth and LFO modulation are not included. PERFORMANCE edit keeps stock's signed depth (+5, -2): it is an amount, not a frequency.
The FX values are worked out from the stock filters' equations and coefficients, at 48 kHz: -3 dB points for HPF and LPF, the shelf's corner for REVERB FRQ. They were not measured with audio.

LPF needs HPF's value: it reads it as the page's graph does, the held trig's or scene's lock when there is one. Where the FX page is not on screen (another view drawing an FX value) LPF shows the stock number.
The 0 to 127 numbers are no longer shown for these knobs.

Two stock sites: param_value_text (0x400a86b4) and the lock box in stock's knob value drawing (0x40037bea). Another module patching either cannot be combined with it. A module that gives these ids its own text through the base's core_params wins over Filter Hz.

claims: ui:FX track DELAY HPF and LPF value text and lock box
ui:FX track REVERB FRQ, HPF and LPF value text and lock box

load.display: None in the audio path: runs only when a frequency value's text or a lock box is drawn
load.conditions: Static: one site is in param_value_text, the routine that formats a parameter's value text for the screen, two in stock's knob value drawing where a locked value's text is placed and its box drawn; nothing is added to the audio, sequencer or tick paths. An FX value's text takes a 28-step CORDIC and, for LPF, a walk of the view stack. Not a measurement.

hardware.summary: On npp1993's Analog Rytm MKII with OS 1.74, FL03 (a Modwerk base development build with Filter Hz 1.3.0, booted from RAM over USB, 2026-11-15) passed seven scripted cases three times, its screens read back from the unit: DELAY and REVERB HPF, LPF and REVERB FRQ in Hz, trig and SCENE locks in wide boxes with LPF following the locked HPF, locked HPF and LPF boxes apart with white around both texts (2.17kHz and 2.21kHz), and PERF edit keeping stock's signed depth.
limitations: Tested by a maintainer, not by the module's porter.
Booted from RAM in a Modwerk base development build; the flash was not written.
FL03: .syx 662563cf8525f9de4e60cf556534ed1692e2ba93dec5a5e958dc8422df810e4e, image CRC 850a1eba read back from the unit.

Screens compared by program against references recorded on the unit; playback while turning was clean on FL01 as reported, other modules beside it, project save and reload, a power cycle and audio were not tried.

tests.summary: 1.3.0: on an Analog Rytm MKII (FL01, RAM boot, 2026-11-15) DELAY and REVERB HPF, LPF and REVERB FRQ read in Hz, trig and scene locks show in wide boxes with LPF following the locked HPF, and PERF edit keeps stock's signed depth; rytm-emu checked every value turned and locked. 1.2.1: the 33-pixel FRQ lock box, checked on a unit (FZ78). 1.2.0: the FRQ popup in Hz on a unit (FZ74, 2026-10-22).
